title: the web shell discards every daemon refusal because it reads a field the daemon does not send
body:
The shell page's client detects daemon refusals by reading `answer.body.error`.
The daemon never sends a field by that name, so NO refusal is ever detected:
the page falls through to the success path and renders an empty form while
the daemon's message and remedy are discarded.

MINE. Landed in 326dbc1f with the browse work. Found while driving `Op::Form`
through the DELIVERED pair (92e4d914a) on vc's instruction -- the drive was
about something else and this fell out of the negative control, which is the
argument for running controls at all.

DRIVEN, against the running daemon, delivered pair 92e4d914a:

    POST /op {"root":"...","op":"form","view":"/thread/ST9999"}
    -> http 200
    {"result":"error","message":"no steel thread ST9999 in this project",
     "remedy":"run `intent st list` to see the threads this project has"}

`wire::Response` is `#[serde(tag = "result", rename_all = "snake_case")]`, so
a refusal is `result: "error"` with the text in `message`. There is no `error`
KEY anywhere in the payload. `answer.body.error` is therefore `undefined` for
every refusal the daemon can produce.

WHAT THE READER SEES, from source (`renderForm`), not from a browser:
`form.entity` and `form.title` are both undefined, so the breadcrumb renders
"intentd / undefined", the `<h1>` renders "undefined", and `(form.fields ||
[])` iterates nothing. A precise, well-authored refusal becomes a blank page
that looks like a broken form.

THE COMMENT DIRECTLY ABOVE THE BUG STATES THE CORRECT RULE: "The daemon
reports its own refusals INSIDE a well-formed response, so a 200 is not on
its own a success and the body is what decides." The reasoning was right and
the field name was wrong, so the guard is PRESENT and aimed at a noun that
does not exist -- the same class as the misaimed `st_show` in 0238, and
invisible to any search for a missing check.

THE `status !== 200` ARM DOES NOT COVER IT and cannot: the daemon
deliberately answers refusals at 200 with the fault inside the body, which is
what the comment is about. So the one branch that could catch this is the one
that is broken.

THE FIX IS ONE PREDICATE -- key on `result === "error"` and read `message`.
It is NOT written yet: filed before fixing, per vc's standing file-then-fix.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT: the web-face tests assert what the DAEMON sends and
the deep-link test asserts the shell is SERVED. Nothing executes the page's
JavaScript, so the client's own branch logic is untested by construction.
Worth saying explicitly rather than leaving as an absence -- whether that
gets a harness is a bigger question than this fix.

RELATED: 0238 (the terminal half of the same "nothing checks existence"
family, now fixed) and 0240 (its unfixed siblings). `intent browse` no longer
composes a URL for a missing entity, so the common route into this state is
closed -- but a bookmark, a reload, or a hand-typed deep link still reaches
it, which is exactly what the deep-link fallback exists to serve.

FIXED 2026-09-04 at 033b4c48d. Suites green: intentsvcs 1196, intent-cli 484,
intentd 26. Both test arms mutation-tested -- restoring the dead branch fails
each with its intended diagnostic.

THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE UNDERSTATED IT, AND cc CORRECTED IT. This filing said the
branch reads the wrong field. It is worse: the branch is DEAD. Because
`answer.body.error` is undefined the guard never fires at all, and the
`status !== 200` guard below cannot catch it either, since refusals are 200 BY
DESIGN. Both guards miss and control reaches `done()` with a refusal in hand,
so the refusal is processed as a SUCCESS. The "undefined over an empty form"
recorded above is what the success renderer produces DOWNSTREAM of the real
fault, not the fault itself.

HALF THE GUESS TYPE-CHECKED AGAINST REALITY, WHICH IS HOW IT SURVIVED A READ
(cc): `remedy` IS a real field on the variant, so the wrong key sat beside a
correct sibling and the line read as checked.

THE FIX IS THREE ORDERED GUARDS, and the order is asserted rather than
assumed. Refusal first, because a refusal arrives at 200. Status second,
because a 401 carries no `result` tag and must be named by its status rather
than by its shape. An unreadable 200 refused last rather than rendered, which
closes the same symptom reached by another route as a CLASS rather than
closing the one instance found.

THE TEST OWNS THE SEAM NOTHING OWNED. Each half was internally consistent --
the daemon serialises its enum correctly, the page reads fields off an object
correctly -- and the defect existed only in the relation between them. The
test serialises the real `wire::Response` and asserts the page reads no field
that no response carries, plus that the refusal's own `message` is read at
all. The second arm matters: a page reading only `result` would pass the
first while still discarding every message.

TWO THINGS THE TEST LEARNED THE HARD WAY, both recorded because they are
reusable. It scans CODE and not COMMENTS -- the first version failed on the
comment explaining the bug, which quotes the dead field by name, and a scanner
that reads prose makes documenting a defect an offence. And it reads the page
at RUNTIME: the compile-time `include_str!` it started with climbed to a
directory between `native/rust` and the repo root, which the shared-artefact
guard's arm 6b mis-resolves by a residual its author had written down in
advance -- and because that guard reads the worktree, an UNTRACKED test file
blocked every commit in the repository for every node until it was parked.

STILL NOT COVERED, and said plainly rather than left as an absence: nothing
executes this page's JavaScript. Its branch logic is untested by construction
and the seam test is what is checkable without a JS engine. Whether the page
gets a real harness is a larger question than this fix and is not decided
here. The fix is also NOT in the delivered pair, which is 92e4d914a.

THE UNCOVERED HALF, RESTATED STRUCTURALLY (vc, 2026-09-04). "Nothing executes
the shell page's JavaScript" reads like a missing test and is not one. It is a
POPULATION THAT CANNOT CONTAIN THE BRANCH LOGIC, BY CONSTRUCTION -- which is
`AC-00.16` arriving on the web face. This defect did not slip past the tests;
it lived in the region no test could reach, and the seam test added here is
precisely the largest checkable subset of that region.

The distinction decides how a later reader should treat it. A DECLARED reach
with an owned gap is the honest state and can be argued about. An UNDECLARED
one is what let a dead branch ship: every existing web-face test asserted what
the DAEMON sends and that the shell is SERVED, all of them green, none of them
able in principle to see the client's own predicate.

A REAL HARNESS FOR THE PAGE IS A SCOPE CALL AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE. It is
hv's, vc is carrying it, and it is recorded on this issue rather than only in
a message so that it cannot go quiet.
